notes.title: SONOKUNI - Gallery Update available now!
notes.notes:
We're excited to announce a new free content update to SONOKUNI! From today, you can dig deep into a vast collection of artwork, design notes, and music tracks as part of a new Gallery Mode. 

Boot up the game from today and you'll find a new option down at the bottom of the main menu. Select that and you'll get to peek behind the curtain to see how the final designs of SONOKUNI came to be, from time-bending power-wielding protagonist Takeru, to the bizarre biotech beings she battles against in her quest for vengeance.


Also included are a collection of music tracks from the game, giving players a chance to aurally drink in the eclectic Japanese hip hop tones of Don Yasa Crew while taking a break from the blood pressure-raising carnage of the main game.


And to celebrate this update - and the critical warmth the game has received since its launch earlier this year - there’s a new Accolades trailer! Check it out below!




[previewyoutube="CxtlczY8g7g;full"][/previewyoutube]


We've been bowled over by the positive response to SONOKUNI so far! As always though, we're keen to hear your feedback - feel free to share your thoughts on the game (or y'know, just give us a follow to find out what we're cooking next) via our socials (Twitter / X | Bluesky | TikTok), or via Steam Discussions.



Many Thanks,



Kakehashi Games

Hi everyone,

We've said it before and we'll say it again: thank you so much to everyone who has picked up SONOKUNI. It's been over a month since launch and we've been blown away by the positive reception!

Special thanks go to everyone that has left a review on Steam as well - every single one counts!

As mentioned in our previous patch note posts, we've got our ears to the ground and are listening to all your feedback. As such, please find the latest patch notes with a few more bug fixes and animation clean-ups below.

Many Thanks,

Kakehashi Games

notes.title: SONOKUNI | Patch notes for 1.0.2
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

Before we get into the details of this 1.0.2 patch for SONOKUNI, we just wanted to say a huge THANK YOU to everyone who has picked up the game and especially to those who have left such awesome feedback. It's been just over a week since launch and we've been blown away by the positive responses (and head bopping emojis).

All that said, if you do have any additional feedback to share, or if you do run into any issues at all, please do feel free to share them with us, either by responding to this post, or by heading to the Steam Discussions board. We are reading everything and every little bit of feedback, no matter how small, helps us improve the game!

Speaking of help, if you haven't already, please do consider leaving SONOKUNI a review on Steam. Getting reviews early doors makes a big difference for plucky hip hop indie games.

Read on for the patch notes!

Many thanks,

Kakehashi Games

***

Patch 1.0.2 notes:

[Difficulty Adjustments]

Bosses


 Second boss stage
 Changed the coloring of bounceable and guardable attacks.


 Third boss stage
 Reduced enemy rotation speed in the first phase.
 Fixed unnatural movement during cutscenes.
 Fixed the hit detection of goldfish bullets and bullet slip (guard) detection.


 Fourth boss stage
 Adjusted the camera work.
 Adjusted the position of enemies that appear from outside the field of view at the bottom of the screen.


[Bug Fixes]

Battle Stages


 Stage 3 (Shrine Stage)
 Fixed an area where it was difficult to distinguish between floors and walls.


 Stage 4 (Public Bath Stage)
 Fixed an area where the main character would get stuck and become trapped.


 Stage 5 (Houseboat Stage)
 Fixed an issue where enemies on Main Route 3 would disappear and the player would become trapped in a room.
 Fixed an issue where players would get trapped by turning back after passing through a room on Main Route 1.


 Common fixes for all stages
 Fixed an issue where leaving the last room without defeating the Wanokuni people would prevent progress.
 Fixed an issue where the image of the defeated main character would show no gore when gore was on.


[Presentation adjustments]

Side-scrolling stage


 Sonokuni
 Fixed a display issue during the prayer cutscene.
 Changed the placement of residents in each stage.


Menus


 Options screen
 Changed the difficulty item on the options screen so that you can check the description.
 Changed the description of the hidden difficulty level so that it is displayed when selecting a chapter.


***

notes.title: Dev update: New track, level transitions, localisations (and new launch window)
notes.notes:
It’s been a busy few months but while we have a little bit of breathing room we wanted to jump into your Steam news feeds with a few updates on Sonokuni, both on development progress and some other news too.

Summer adventures

Over the Summer we took Sonokuni to Bitsummit, where it won two (!) awards: Excellence in Sound Design and VGC’s Media Highlight Award. Sonokuni was also playable on the show floor at Tokyo Games Show.

We wanted, first and foremost, to send out a huge ‘thank you’ to everyone who came along to the Kakehashi Games booths at these events and played the game. It was awesome to get some direct feedback (and of course great to see heads bopping along to the beat!).

Laying down tracks

Back at Don Yasa Crew HQ, the development team x J-hip hop crew has been busy implementing a lot of new things in the game. Not least a bunch of new tracks for the later levels.

Check out 'DO', one of these new tracks in full below - headphones/full volume recommended:

[previewyoutube=VKQg_ND27nI;full][/previewyoutube]

Getting around

Don Yasa Crew are keen to show a little more of the surrounding world of the game outside of the titular village of ‘Sonokuni’ and the neighbouring country of ‘Wanokuni’ (where the stages take place). With this in mind they have now added a characteristically psychedelic array of transition sequences. The aim here is to gently hint at the state of the world outside of these two main locations. We hope you find these sequences intriguing and a little surprising!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42598993/bf34b3c1505c4fc0c7c021ea1ba56ba8c59967b7.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42598993/0e1fad515cc3bf7fba2208834a08a53c178e21f6.gif

Translations inbound

One of the questions we are most asked is whether Sonokuni will be fully localised into XYZ language. We’re happy to give you a little peek behind the curtain at the localisation progress being made. The current ‘in development’ build is now playable in English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Russian.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42598993/154549f3f11d3290d2e9b542abf7184fff339d11.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42598993/173b1d879e58c09083be40d71280bf047a61adf4.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42598993/80cb5c3535570ac20d2879490a3f45e67c43e491.png

Launch window update

A key thing we wanted to tell you about as well is that, while development is coming along really well so far, we’ve made the decision to shift the expected launch window back into early 2025. 

We were previously aiming to have Sonokuni in your hands by the end of this year, but after having so many people playing the game during the various events and the Steam Next Fest demo earlier in the year, we’ve received so much awesome feedback it would be a shame not to include in the final game due to time constraints.

We’re sorry to have to push the release back like this, though we’re confident that this is the right thing to do to ensure we have all the time needed to create the best, most well-balanced, and polished version of Sonokuni possible.

***

Thanks for taking the time to read through this update, and for your interest in Sonokuni! Please do consider wishlisting if you haven’t already (this stuff really does help!). And of course keep an eye out - and an ear open - for more updates.

The Kakehashi Games Team
